summary: @servicetitan/anvil-icon preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: Package publishes as an SVG icon set (`files: mdi/{filled,outlined,round,sharp,two-tone}/*.svg`) but its `package.json` declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. `setup.mjs` is obfuscated (hex-identifier `_0x...` naming) and, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<pm>.zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync("bun", [path.join(D, "math_init.js")], {stdio:"inherit", cwd:D})`. The bundled `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line CJS payload (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with a rotated string-array (`n7gIxM=[...]`), array-rotation function `WV8StW`, and decoder `hc1jfK9`; its behavior cannot be resolved without executing the decoder. Fetching a second runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated bundle at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern, unrelated to shipping SVG icons. The scoped name `@servicetitan/*` with no source, no README, and generic gitHead is consistent with a dependency-confusion lure targeting the private ServiceTitan scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
